title: Rhinitis, Supplements and a Passport Video Post-Mortem
titleZh: 鼻炎、补剂与护照视频复盘
description: Steven recovers from rhinitis and looks at how his "Is a passport really necessary?" video did across six platforms, where it earned 19 cents in total. He also explains why he's sticking with his online backup plan, corrects Xiaomi founder Lei Jun's name, and walks through his new supplement routine of red ginseng, pea protein and creatine.

sentences.zh: 本期速览
sentences.en: Episode at a Glance

sentences.zh: 史蒂文从几天的鼻炎困扰中恢复过来，迎来了满满一天的训练、内容创作和"拿自己做实验"。
sentences.en: Steven recovered from several days of sinus trouble and had a packed day of training, content creation, and "experimenting on himself."

sentences.zh: 他盘点了《护照真的必要吗？
sentences.en: He reviewed how his video "Is a Passport Really Necessary?

sentences.zh: 》这个视频在六个平台上的反响，讲解了自己"直播剪片子"的工作流程，也反思了为什么明明网络副业还没能取代教书收入，自己却还在坚持做下去。
sentences.en: " was received across six platforms, explained his workflow for "editing videos live," and reflected on why he keeps at it even though his online side business still hasn't replaced his teaching income.

sentences.zh: 另外，他纠正了昨天节目里说错的一个名字，还深入聊了聊自己为了周五重返工作岗位而调整的"补剂配方"。
sentences.en: He also corrected a name he got wrong in yesterday's episode, and talked in depth about the "supplement formula" he has adjusted for his return to work on Friday.

sentences.zh: 鼻炎、毛线帽，化学药 vs. 天然偏方
sentences.en: Rhinitis, wool hats, chemical drugs vs. natural home remedies

sentences.zh: 今天史蒂文感觉好多了——他的鼻炎老毛病在加拿大和中国都反反复复发作，他自己也说不清到底是灰尘、天气，还是忘了戴毛线帽闹的。
sentences.en: Steven is feeling much better today. His chronic rhinitis keeps flaring up in both Canada and China, and even he can't say for sure whether it's caused by dust, the weather, or forgetting to wear his wool hat.

sentences.zh: 他买了一款中国的非处方喷鼻剂（二丙酸倍氯米松），纠结了一番"化学减充血剂"和薄荷、尤加利这类天然偏方之间的取舍：天然的只能暂时通气，并不能真正消炎。
sentences.en: He bought a Chinese over-the-counter nasal spray (beclomethasone dipropionate) and went back and forth over the trade-off between "chemical decongestants" and natural remedies like peppermint and eucalyptus: natural ones only clear the nose temporarily and don't really reduce the inflammation.

sentences.zh: 他还把这事和自己戒酒的经历做了类比：“你能接受每天用化学喷鼻剂，就像每天喝一杯啤酒那样，对身体造成化学性损害吗？”
sentences.en: He also compared it to his own experience of quitting drinking: "Can you accept using a chemical nasal spray every day, just like drinking a beer every day, and the chemical damage that does to your body?"

sentences.zh: 《护照真的必要吗？》——各平台反响大盘点
sentences.en: "Is a Passport Really Necessary?" — A Roundup of Reactions Across Platforms

sentences.zh: YouTube Shorts上这个视频只有1800次观看，评论大多是批评（有观众还以为他是美国人——“你怎么敢这么说？”
sentences.en: On YouTube Shorts this video got only 1,800 views, and most comments were critical (some viewers even thought he was American — "How dare you say that?"

sentences.zh: Instagram有2000到2500次观看，互动最积极；TikTok和小红书几乎没人看；反倒是Snapchat悄悄拿下3000次观看的"冠军"。
sentences.en: Instagram got 2,000 to 2,500 views with the most positive engagement; almost nobody watched it on TikTok or Xiaohongshu; surprisingly, Snapchat quietly took the "crown" with 3,000 views.

sentences.zh: 至于赚钱嘛，目前只有YouTube有收益——这条视频一共赚了19美分。
sentences.en: As for making money, so far only YouTube has paid out — this video earned a total of 19 cents.

sentences.zh: YouTube：1800次观看，11条评论，收益0.19美元
sentences.en: YouTube: 1,800 views, 11 comments, $0.19 in earnings

sentences.zh: Instagram：2000-2500次观看，评论最正面
sentences.en: Instagram: 2,000–2,500 views, the most positive comments

sentences.zh: Snapchat：3000次观看，暂无收益统计
sentences.en: Snapchat: 3,000 views, no earnings data yet

sentences.zh: TikTok／小红书：流量都很惨淡
sentences.en: TikTok / Xiaohongshu: traffic was dismal on both

sentences.zh: 直播与"内容驻军"
sentences.en: Live streams and "content garrisoning"

sentences.zh: 史蒂文今天开了TikTok直播和Substack直播两场，顺带解释了自己的创作流程：先录播客 → 发到TikTok（用来试水、内容转瞬即逝）→ 用ChatGPT打磨文字稿 → 用Gamma App做成幻灯片 → 最后搬到Substack直播留档（但这个平台不太适合剪片，因为屏幕共享时他自己被挤到角落一小块）。
sentences.en: Today Steven did two live streams, one on TikTok and one on Substack, and along the way explained his creative workflow: first record the podcast → post it to TikTok (to test the waters; content there is fleeting) → polish the transcript with ChatGPT → turn it into slides with Gamma App → finally move it to a Substack live stream for the record (though that platform isn't great for clipping, because during screen sharing he gets squeezed into a small corner).

sentences.zh: 他开始怀疑是不是该在这么多平台同时发力，毕竟观众本来就不多，哪个平台漏看一条评论其实也无所谓。
sentences.en: He's starting to wonder whether he should really be pushing on so many platforms at once; after all, his audience is small to begin with, so missing a comment on one platform or another doesn't really matter.

sentences.zh: 为什么还要坚持下去？"备用计划"的逻辑
sentences.en: Why keep going? The logic of a "backup plan"

sentences.zh: 这整个YouTube／Substack／TikTok项目最初的目的有两个：一是给自己的语言学习进度留个"证据"，二是攒一个收入备用计划，因为他的中国签证是绑在大学教职上的。
sentences.en: This whole YouTube/Substack/TikTok project originally had two goals: first, to leave "evidence" of his own language-learning progress, and second, to build up a backup income plan, because his Chinese visa is tied to his university teaching job.

sentences.zh: 他给自己定的目标是6月底前实现盈利——结果没实现，但他还是咬牙坚持，理由是内容库攒得够多，总有一天能赢得算法的信任。
sentences.en: The goal he set himself was to become profitable by the end of June. He didn't make it, but he gritted his teeth and kept going, reasoning that once he had built up a big enough content library, he would eventually win the algorithm's trust.

sentences.zh: “也可能是因为……史蒂文，你这老师当得太烂了，这也是个可能的原因。”
sentences.en: "Or maybe it's because… Steven, you're just a really terrible teacher. That's a possible reason too."

sentences.zh: 重返工作、发薪日，还有房租的"时间差"
sentences.en: Back to work, payday, and the rent "timing gap"

sentences.zh: 国庆黄金周今天结束，周五就要恢复教课，之后要连上十二周才到期末考试，中间再没有假期。
sentences.en: The National Day Golden Week ends today; classes resume on Friday, and after that there are twelve straight weeks until final exams, with no more holidays in between.

sentences.zh: 他5号刚发了工资，却发现房租居然要在发薪日前七天就交——也就是说，10月的工资（11月5日才到账）得用来付11月底的房租。
sentences.en: He just got paid on the 5th, but discovered that rent is actually due seven days before payday — which means October's salary (which only arrives on November 5) has to pay for rent at the end of November.

sentences.zh: 他把这事和之前一家公司对比，那家公司是延后60天发薪的。
sentences.en: He compared this with a previous company, which paid salaries 60 days late.

sentences.zh: 另外，他还提到欠尼亚加拉报社一个月的稿子还没写，以及同事每年例行的"我明年肯定辞职"倒计时。
sentences.en: He also mentioned that he still hasn't written the month's worth of articles he owes the Niagara newspaper, as well as his colleague's yearly ritual countdown of "I'm definitely quitting next year."

sentences.zh: 更正：是雷军，不是"韦军"——汉字也会"过期"
sentences.en: Correction: it's Lei Jun, not "Wei Jun" — Chinese characters can "expire" too

sentences.zh: 昨天说错的"韦军"其实是雷军，小米创始人。
sentences.en: The "Wei Jun" I wrongly mentioned yesterday is actually Lei Jun, the founder of Xiaomi.

sentences.zh: 史蒂文借这个口误聊开了一个有趣的话题：汉字的读音和用法有时会被官方重新"解释"或改写（他举例说参议员卢比奥据称被重新批准入境中国时，名字被改成了"卢比奥"的新写法），他总结道：“今天你还认得这个汉字，明天可能就不认得了。”
sentences.en: Steven used this slip of the tongue to open up an interesting topic: the pronunciation and usage of Chinese characters are sometimes officially "reinterpreted" or rewritten (as an example, he said that when Senator Rubio was reportedly re-approved for entry into China, his name was changed to a new way of writing "Rubio"), and he concluded: "Today you still recognize this character; tomorrow you might not."

sentences.zh: 补剂配方大改造
sentences.en: A major overhaul of the supplement formula

sentences.zh: 史蒂文打算用高丽红参取代吃了一年效果不明显的玛咖（本来是用来提升性欲和认知的），他认为红参更接近中医范畴，对提升性欲和情绪更有帮助。
sentences.en: Steven plans to replace maca, which he has taken for a year without noticeable results (it was originally meant to boost libido and cognition), with Korean red ginseng. He thinks red ginseng is closer to the realm of Chinese medicine and more helpful for boosting libido and mood.

sentences.zh: 他还加了一款豌豆蛋白粉（灵感来自生物黑客布莱恩·约翰逊），这次是在本地买的，而不是冒险从加拿大"人肉带货"。
sentences.en: He also added a pea protein powder (inspired by biohacker Bryan Johnson), and this time he bought it locally instead of risking "smuggling it in his luggage" from Canada.

sentences.zh: 另外，他时隔十年又小心翼翼地重新开始吃一水肌酸（Creapure），每天只吃3克，配咖啡服用，并打算一周只吃两三次而不是每天吃，免得身体过度依赖那种"充血膨胀"的外观效果。
sentences.en: In addition, after a ten-year gap he has cautiously started taking creatine monohydrate (Creapure) again, only 3 grams a day with coffee, and he plans to take it only two or three times a week instead of daily, so his body doesn't become overly dependent on that "pumped, bloated" look.

sentences.zh: 今日总结
sentences.en: Today's summary

sentences.zh: 史蒂文今天的主线很清楚：从化学喷鼻剂到肌酸热潮，再到汉字规则的变来变去，凡事都要多问一句"真的是这样吗"，然后自己去查证，而不是盲目相信任何单一信息来源——哪怕是AI。
sentences.en: Steven's main thread today is clear: from chemical nasal sprays to the creatine craze, and on to Chinese character rules that keep changing, you should always ask one more time "Is that really so?" and then check it yourself, instead of blindly trusting any single source of information — even AI.
